title: Loongson 2K1000 real-board Git validation
current_state: Work continues on branch feature/portable-net-vf2-dwmac from the LA QEMU SMP4 shootdown checkpoint 0f8b3315; commits 521c2114 and 0811e354 remain the shared Pmap/TLB baseline and were not reverted or duplicated.

Stages 1 through 4 are complete on real Loongson 2K1000 Nebula hardware: the independent la64-2k1000 target boots both cores through the common kernel path, preserves real IOCSR IPI/generation shootdown/UART LIOINTC behavior, reads the onboard SATA disk through ls-ahci, mounts its raw ext4 filesystem as /, and enters the Alpine / #.
U-Boot 2022.04-v2.1.0-00579-g3bcf8c7d reports 1 GiB DDR in two banks: 0x9000000000000000+256 MiB and 0x9000000090000000+768 MiB. Its TFTP staging loadaddr is 0x9000000098000000.

The Stage 3 legacy uImage contains 7032768 payload bytes with 32-bit physical load/entry 0x98000000. Its 64-byte header is transported at cached alias 0x9000000097ffffc0, so the vendor U-Boot relocation maps source and destination to the same pointer. The linked kernel ends at physical 0x98761000 before the initrd header at 0x98800000.

The real-board two-argument bootm run verified both image CRCs, reported 1024 MiB, printed the inherited/reinitialized UART markers, recovered a 100 MHz CPUCFG timebase and raw CPIO range 0x98800040..0x98963640 from the BPI EFI FDT, emitted boot:ok, and entered / #.

The board entry installs VSEG9 cached and VSEG8 uncached DMWs, sets CRMD IE=0/DA=0/PG=1, invalidates TLB only after reaching the high DMW, and drives the NS16550A at physical 0x1fe20000 from the 125 MHz APB clock. Stage 3 releases CPU1 through the vendor mailbox into a separate high trampoline/stack, then enables CPU-local timer/IPI plus the proven CPU0 HWI1 UART cascade.

BootInfo publishes physical RAM banks 0..0x10000000 and 0x90000000..0xc0000000 while reserving the fixed FDT scratch, framebuffer shared-dma-pool, bootparam area, linked kernel, and initrd. Firmware pointers accept only raw physical or known cached/uncached DMW forms; FDT totalsize, UTF-8 cmdline, and initrd overlaps are checked before unsafe parsing or publication.

The live control FDT, not the empty SPI dtb partition, is the current hardware source of truth. Confirmed nodes include the 2K1000 ICU, ls-ahci at 0x400e0000 IRQ19, and two DWMAC 3.70a controllers; GMAC1 at 0x40050000 is the U-Boot path that links at 1000/full.
The SATA device is a Kingchuxing 32GB disk containing a raw ext4 filesystem at LBA0 with no partition table; U-Boot ext4ls scsi 0:0 / succeeds. No disk image or mother rootfs was modified.

Stage 4 adds a generic read-only AHCI polling driver and a board-local resource binding for MMIO 0x400e0000, hwirq19/public IRQ20, and the 32-bit coherent identity DMA domain. txKernel identifies 62533296 512-byte blocks, registers sda/DevT(8,0), validates the ext4 superblock, mounts tx.root=sda directly as a read-only root, honors init=/bin/sh, and reaches the Alpine / # without issuing disk writes.

The Stage 4 BSS corruption was a generic ext4 stack overflow, not DMA: the 512-entry inline lookup cache made Ext4FsInstance::open_with_backend_planner_and_mapping reserve 66448 bytes on the 65536-byte board boot stack. Moving the entry store to a heap Vec reduced the LA debug stack frame to 928 bytes and preserved the boot command line.

The LA page-table, ASID, trap, per-CPU, unaligned-access, architectural IOCSR IPI, and generation-based TLB shootdown sources now live in a platform-neutral tx-hal-loongarch64-common source directory. QEMU keeps its slave-ROM boot mailbox and ExtIOI/PCH implementation separate and passed a fresh four-vCPU BusyBox run with bidirectional IPI, masked-progress shootdown, and boot sentinels.

Real hardware reports possible=2, online-aps=1, online=2, and iocsr-ipi=yes. BSP-to-AP and AP-to-BSP IPI, ordinary and interrupt-masked generation shootdown, reactor AP execution, owner-wake, and RCU SMP sentinels all pass without a global serialization lock or permanent wait.

The old firmware DTS describes LIOINTC main 0x1fe01400 with a CPU IRQ3/HWI1 cascade. The board maps public IRQ as hwirq+1, routes only the shared UART0..3 source hwirq0 to CPU0/HWI1 with route byte 0x21, disables the other UART IERs and all unowned LIOINTC sources, and has a real first-RX irq:uart-rx:ok witness. QEMU ExtIOI/PCH addresses are not reused.

The previous 0x1fe01020..0x1fe01038 ICU interpretation was rejected: those registers are vendor SMP mailboxes. The per-core +0x44 readback remains undocumented and is not used by the driver; the proven UART-only claim path reads global status masked by enable status.

The live /proc/cpuinfo now enumerates CPU0 and CPU1 as architecture loongarch64 from a dynamic platform provider; the former RV64 placeholder is gone while the RV64 text remains byte-compatible in its own target.

Stage 5 is next: bring up the live-FDT DWMAC 3.70a GMAC path, including controller selection, PHY/MDIO, clock/reset, coherent DMA descriptors and the source-specific LIOINTC route. Do not reuse the VF2 DWMAC5/EQoS register model or QEMU network constants without capability checks.
Do not write or reorganize the LA knowledge handbook while bringing the board up. Complete the hardware chain first; documentation is a separate user-directed task afterward.

caveats: Never print, log, document, stage, or commit the PAT stored in local-images/git/launch-shell.sh. The local-images directory is ignored and the helper is not tracked.
Do not modify the competition LA rootfs mother image during experiments; use a copy or a disposable overlay when the transport permits it.
QEMU 10.0.2.2/10.0.2.3 networking values are QEMU user-network endpoints and must not be copied to the physical 2K1000 network configuration.
U-Boot and txKernel may program different IP and MAC values while taking turns controlling the same physical Ethernet hardware; U-Boot network state does not automatically carry into txKernel.
Keep commands short: avoid unnecessary shell variables, if branches, printf scaffolding, generated helper scripts, and destructive cleanup commands.

The verified LIOINTC setup owns the shared UART hwirq0 route. Stage 4 models AHCI hwirq19/public IRQ20 as level-high but deliberately leaves it masked because the accepted bootstrap transport is polling; GMAC IRQs still need source-specific routing and live verification before unmasking.
The one-time irq:uart-rx:ok line is the real-board proof that the first console byte traversed LIOINTC/HWI1; later input uses the same IRQ path with the existing polling reader only as fallback.
For every hardware step, identify the execution context, show the shortest command, show only the key success output, and state what failure means.
Do not describe intermediate repair history in user-facing knowledge documents. Record the final working chain and durable constraints only.
